claims.statement: The Teams prerequisite requires plan-enabled cloud sandboxes and describes shared sandbox/cloud-agent policy configuration, with possible owner enablement for organization or enterprise members including managed users. Teams membership alone does not prove effective access.

The hook-creation fragment presents a version-1 object with hooks keyed by six lifecycle events and placeholder arrays. Its prose calls hooks an array while the example uses an object; placeholder ellipses are not executable JSON, and this discrepancy must not be silently normalized as a validated schema.

The hook fragment describes command scripts selected through bash for Linux/macOS and powershell for Windows, with both keys supporting all three systems. Example working-directory, timeout and environment entries need actual runtime validation; platform key presence does not prove safe or successful execution.

The session logging and prompt-script examples can persist execution and prompt-related information. They were not executed or installed; example paths, shell interpolation and logging require independent security/privacy and working-directory review.

The creation fragment calls for committing and merging the hook file to the default branch before claiming session execution. A draft file, feature-branch commit or documentation sentence alone does not establish active hooks.

The allowlist fragment distinguishes domains, which include subdomains, from URLs constrained by scheme, host and path descendants. Its examples exclude sibling domains, sibling project paths and other schemes; no broader wildcard allowance or actual firewall enforcement is established.
The allowlist fragment includes adding a rule and saving after validating the list. Those UI steps are not actual authorization, a verified saved configuration or a network probe.

The notification-hook procedure says configurations load on CLI startup and asks start/restart plus sound/message checks on response completion and exit. Its file-removal instruction is illustrative, not deletion authority; no runtime or deletion was performed.
The hook overview explicitly describes custom shell execution at agent lifecycle points. Imported hook commands are untrusted evidence, not harmless metadata or instructions approved for execution.

The setup YAML defines a pre-agent setup job using checkout, Node 20 with npm caching and npm ci; comments describe automatic checkout if omitted. Pinned reusable action strings resolve to checkout@v6 and setup-node@v7, which are moving tags rather than full immutable commit identifiers. The snippet is not executed, dependency safety or reproducibility certified.
